verses.text: In the 1631 print of the King James Version, the commandment in Exodus 20:14 saying “Thou shalt not commit adultery” has been accidentally rendered as “Thou shalt commit adultery,” omitting the word not. Its printers Robert Barker, who before printed the 1611 KJV, and Martin Lucas were summoned to court before King Charles I for this mistake, fined £300 (= ca. £63,000 in 2023), and stripped of their printing licenses. Very few of these 1631 KJV prints have survived, and specimen are only to be found in the US, UK, and Ireland, though rumours surround many of them. Bonhams in London, England auctioned one specimen in November 11, 2015 for an asking price of £10,000 to £15,000. Another specimen allegedly found its way to New Zealand in 2018, and The Guardian published an article on it in 2022. The 1631 KJV is now called the “Wicked Bible” or “Sinners Bible”.
